Relief has never run against the live machine, only against fakes

findings.text: Relief's "still over the line after the run" check reads the same monitor snapshot it started from (`Servex/Relief.js:308` calls `commit_pct()`, which reads `procmon.commit_mb`, and that only changes on the monitor's next 10 s PowerShell tick). So the risk note fires on every first run of every episode, however much relief freed. Wait for the next procmon `tick` (or check on Relief's next minute) before deciding. The test "relief that gets the commit under the line posts no note" passes only because its fake sweep changes `commit_mb` synchronously.

Most of the drop from 726 kept to 7 kept is relabelling. `Lifecycle.sweep()` now returns dormant agent rows apart as `dormant` (`Servex/Lifecycle.js:442-443`), but the `lifecycle-sweep` log line (`Servex/Servex.js:1591`) still writes only `kept: r.kept.length`. About 670 dormant rows now vanish from the log. Add `dormant: r.dormant` to that line; it was outside this fence, so it is a follow-up.

The STANDING regex now exists three times: `Servex/agents/Agents.js:1243`, `Servex/Processes.js:267`, and a new copy at `Servex/Relief.js:225`. A future edit to one will miss the others. Move it to a small SDK-free module that all three import.

The brief said Relief is "ticked once a minute from the monitor". It runs its own `setInterval` instead (`Servex/Relief.js:248`), like Games.js does. That works, but it is a different shape from what was asked.

`freed_mb_estimate` adds `row.mb` for each Lifecycle close row (`Servex/Relief.js:279`). The agent rows built at `Servex/Lifecycle.js:262` carry no `mb`, so closed agents add 0 and the estimate runs low.

`remove()`'s new guard (`Servex/Pool.js:547-551`) applies to every caller that does not pass force. I checked them: sweep (ready slots), hold's "one ready is enough", reclaim's dead-server removal, and recycle_orphans (state `orphan`) all still pass the guard, so none of the self-heal paths are blocked.
